The second alpha of the **IdeaBlade Validation Editor**, a desktop editor for [IdeaBlade Validation](https://github.com/Breeze/ideablade-validation)'s validation metadata. This one is about finding your way around large projects, and sources taken from whole folders.

> **Note:** What you see here was written in a few hours with the help of [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code). The code hasn't been fully reviewed and vetted. It's meant as a developer tool, not a fully fleshed-out production app.

## Downloads

| | Download | Installing |
|---|---|---|
| **Windows** (x64) | [IdeaBlade-Validation-Editor-Setup-0.1.0-alpha.2.exe](https://github.com/Breeze/ideablade-validation-editor/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.2/IdeaBlade-Validation-Editor-Setup-0.1.0-alpha.2.exe) | Run it. It's not code-signed, so SmartScreen may warn: *More info* → *Run anyway*. It installs for everyone (Program Files, with an administrator prompt) or only for you, over alpha.1 if that's installed. |

It's not signed with an Apple certificate or notarized, so the first time, right-click the app → *Open* → *Open* (or run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "/Applications/IdeaBlade Validation Editor.app"`). |

| **Linux** (x64) | [IdeaBlade-Validation-Editor-0.1.0-alpha.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage](https://github.com/Breeze/ideablade-validation-editor/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.2/IdeaBlade-Validation-Editor-0.1.0-alpha.2-linux-x86_64.AppImage) | `chmod +x` it and run it. |
| **Linux**, Debian or Ubuntu (x64) | [IdeaBlade-Validation-Editor-0.1.0-alpha.2-linux-amd64.deb](https://github.com/Breeze/ideablade-validation-editor/releases/download/v0.1.0-alpha.2/IdeaBlade-Validation-Editor-0.1.0-alpha.2-linux-amd64.deb) | `sudo apt install ./IdeaBlade-Validation-Editor-0.1.0-alpha.2-linux-amd64.deb` |

The Windows installer was checked on Windows 11. The macOS and Linux builds come from GitHub's runners and haven't been tried on those systems yet: please open an issue if they don't start.

## What's new since alpha.1

- **Sources from a folder.** **Add folder…** (Ctrl+Shift+M) adds a folder's TypeScript and C# files, in it and its subfolders, as a pattern (`<folder>/**/*.{ts,cs}`). New files are picked up as they're written, and deleted ones go. In the Sources list a pattern is one entry, folded by default, with its file count; ✎ changes it (to `server/Dtos/Admin/*.cs`, say) and ✕ removes it with its files. Patterns are saved to the project file as patterns.
- **Find model types and maps.** A search field above the list (also View → Find Model Type or Map, Ctrl+Shift+F) narrows it as you type, marking the matching part; Enter opens the first match, Esc clears it. Clearing it keeps what you selected in view, and opening another project clears it.
- **Folding.** Files and maps fold with the ▾ before their names; **Collapse all** and **Expand all** fold or open every file and map. What's folded is remembered for each project.
- **A sidebar that stays put.** The project, the Metadata heading and the search are pinned at the top, the sources and settings at the bottom, and the list scrolls between them.
- **Add where you are.** Each map's "model type…" field and each TS or C# file's "Add map" now come first, above the model types and maps, and stay while you search: find a file by one of its model types and add another to it there. What you add stays in view until the search is cleared.
- **Two sample projects** in `samples/`: `large-project` (13 metadata files, about 200 model types) and `folder-sources` (folders of TS view models and C# DTOs).

One change in behaviour: a pattern in a project file used to be dropped on saving when none of the files it matched were loaded. Now a pattern stays until you remove it.

See the [README](https://github.com/Breeze/ideablade-validation-editor/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.2/README.md) for the details, [alpha.1's notes](https://github.com/Breeze/ideablade-validation-editor/releases/tag/v0.1.0-alpha.1) for everything that was in the first alpha, and the [library's documentation](https://github.com/Breeze/ideablade-validation/tree/main/docs) for the metadata itself.
